title: Todo List
story: You wake up to a flood of notifications: 'Submit report,' 'Buy groceries,' 'Call dentist,' 'Fix bug #437.' Your brain can't track all this. You need a todo list that lets you add tasks, mark them complete, and see what's left.
why: Managing items in a Vec — add, remove by index, list remaining — is the foundation of task tracking and list-based applications.
analogy: A todo list Vec is like sticky notes on a wall. You add new notes (push), read them left to right (for loop), and peel one off when done (pop or remove-by-index). The wall only holds what's still pending.
try_it: Add a `priority` field by storing tasks as `"HIGH: Submit report"` — then sort high-priority tasks to the top. Add a function that counts how many tasks are remaining. Try to add a `clear_all` function that removes every task from the Vec.
tips: Use `.pop()` to remove from the end when order doesn't matter — it's simpler than rebuilding the Vec
Number tasks starting at 1 (human-friendly) even though Vec indices start at 0 (computer-friendly)
Keep display logic separate from data logic — one function prints, another modifies
common_mistakes: Removing an item from the middle of a Vec shifts all later items left — index numbers change after removal
Re-printing the entire list for every operation instead of just printing once after all changes
Forgetting that `.pop()` returns `Option[Str]` — you must handle the case where the list is empty
